passage:
Three offers had come in, and the whole house in Nashik seemed to have an opinion. Tanuja's uncle read the numbers aloud at lunch. "The Gurgaon one pays the most. That's the one."

"But it's a sales role," Tanuja said. "The other is in Pune, in a small design studio, and the team seemed kind."

Her aunt Zeenat looked up from the rice. "Beta, we're only saying it because of your father's loan. Money is safe."

Tanuja felt a lump in her throat. She heard the worry beneath the pushing, and it was real. She also knew that she had barely slept the whole week before her last sales interview.

"I'll list what each one gives me, not just the salary," she said. "Learning, the city, how the team treated me. I'll decide by Sunday."

Zeenat nodded slowly, and passed her the dal.

qa.q: Which offer did Tanuja's uncle want her to take, and why?
qa.a: The uncle wanted her to take the Gurgaon offer because it pays the most.

qa.q: What was Zeenat worried about when she said money is safe?
qa.a: Zeenat was worried about the father's loan and felt money was safe, so the push came from care.

qa.q: How did Tanuja handle the pressure well?
qa.a: Tanuja listened to the worry, then said she would list what each offer gave her beyond salary, such as learning, the city and the team, and decide by Sunday.

qa.q: How might the uncle feel if Tanuja chose the Pune studio?
qa.a: The uncle might feel anxious about the loan and the future, but a clear list of reasons could help him see it as a considered choice rather than carelessness.

grounding: Relatives push Tanuja to take the highest bid; she hears the worry behind it and weighs growth, health and culture alongside salary.

passage:
I'm Farida, and last winter every aunt in the family had an opinion about my two offers. One from a consulting firm in Dubai with the bigger package. One from a housing nonprofit in Bhopal, where I'd grown up, with less money but real work on the projects I cared about.
Jyoti-phuppo called me every evening. "Take Dubai. Your father worked so hard. Why would you choose less?" I felt guilty. I also felt furious, and then guilty for being furious.
It took me a week to hear what was under it. My phuppo had seen my father work double shifts to pay my fees. She was scared for me, not controlling me.
So I told her plainly: "Phuppo, I'm choosing the job where I'll learn and stay healthy. I know you worry. I'll show you the plan." She was quiet, then said, "Just promise me you'll eat properly." I promised.

qa.a: In Bhopal, where Farida had grown up.

qa.q: What was Farida feeling during Jyoti-phuppo's calls?
qa.a: Farida felt guilty and furious, and then guilty again for being furious.

qa.q: How did Farida make the decision while respecting the family's worry?
qa.a: Farida saw the fear behind the pressure, weighed growth and health along with pay, and explained the choice plainly with a plan.

qa.q: How might Jyoti-phuppo see Farida's choice at the end?
qa.a: She may still feel anxious, but her request to eat properly shows she accepts the choice and simply wants Farida to be safe.

grounding: Relatives push the protagonist to take the highest-paying offer; she hears the worry behind it and weighs growth and health too.

passage:
Placement counsellor's note, 2 p.m.
Indu came in with her uncle Gautam, who did most of the talking. "Two offers. One pays more, in Chennai. Why is she even thinking about the other?"
Indu sat with her arms folded. When I asked her directly, she said the Chennai role meant night shifts in a call centre, and the other, at a Mysuru design studio, meant training in her real field. She added, quietly, that she had been ill last year after months of irregular sleep.
Mr Gautam was worried, I could see, about her mother's expenses since her father passed away. I told him his worry made sense. Then I asked Indu to list what each job would give her in three years, not only what it paid.
She chose to take a day. Mr Gautam shook my hand on the way out and said, "I just want her secure." Indu touched his arm. I will check in with her on Thursday.

qa.q: What did the Chennai role involve?
qa.a: Night shifts in a call centre.

qa.q: How can you tell Indu felt pressured at the start?
qa.a: She sat with her arms folded while her uncle did most of the talking, showing she felt uneasy and unheard.

qa.q: How did the counsellor help Indu weigh the offers?
qa.a: The counsellor validated Mr Gautam's worry and asked Indu to list what each job would give her in three years, beyond pay.

qa.q: How might Mr Gautam see Indu's hesitation?
qa.a: He is anxious about the family's expenses and wants her secure, so he may see the lower offer as a risk rather than a choice about growth and health.

grounding: Relatives push the protagonist toward the highest offer; she hears the worry behind it and weighs growth and health as well as salary.
